SETTINGS_TICK_RES_HIGH: High precision (1 ns · up to 500 MHz)
SETTINGS_TICK_RES_DEFAULT_DESC: Backwards-compatible with existing snapshots and lessons. Fastest runs and lowest memory. Clocks above 50 MHz alias down to 50 MHz.
SETTINGS_TICK_RES_HIGH_DESC: Accurate visualisation up to 500 MHz. Expect ~10x slower simulations and ~10x more signal-history memory per run.
SETTINGS_TICK_RES_ADAPTIVE_DESC: Picks the coarsest tick that still gives at least two ticks per clock period. Only pays the precision cost when the effective clock needs it.

HOME_TITLE: Kmila-9s: A Multiplatform VHDL Learning and Debugging Tool
HOME_SUBTITLE: An application for learning and debugging VHDL code without requiring physical hardware.
HOME_OVERVIEW_P1: Kmila-9s is a multiplatform desktop application, running in a local environment, aimed at debugging VHDL (VHSIC Hardware Description Language) code. Its objective is to facilitate the analysis of programs through simulation and interactive visualization of digital signals, clock cycles, and port states.
HOME_OVERVIEW_P2: The project aims to support the academic learning of digital design for FPGAs (Field Programmable Gate Arrays), offering a free and open-source tool that strengthens educational practices and allows for a practical understanding of the logic of digital systems without requiring physical hardware.
HOME_FEATURE_VISUALIZATION_DESC: Observe the states of signals, ports, and internal variables at any time.
HOME_FEATURE_CROSSPLATFORM_DESC: Runs on Windows, macOS, Android, iOS, iPadOS, and Linux (via web).
HOME_FEATURE_OFFLINE_DESC: Works locally without an internet connection.
HOME_FEATURE_PRELAB_DESC: Prepare for physical lab sessions in advance.
HOME_FEATURE_ACCESSIBILITY_DESC: Study from any computer or mobile device.
HOME_FEATURE_PROTOTYPING_DESC: Validate designs faster than with traditional methods.

LEARN_SUBTITLE: From your very first bit to a pipelined CPU — guided readings, worked samples, fix-the-bug exercises, and full projects. Track your progress and open anything straight into the Kmila editor.

LEARN_TRACK_BEGINNER_BLURB: Binary, boolean algebra, gates — the mental model you need before you write a single line of VHDL.
LEARN_TRACK_EASY_BLURB: VHDL syntax, combinational design, simulation. Short lessons, one concept each.
LEARN_TRACK_INTERMEDIATE_BLURB: Processes, flip-flops, counters, finite-state machines — the moment static circuits start to remember.
LEARN_TRACK_ADVANCED_BLURB: Memories, ALUs, small CPUs, bus protocols. Multi-module designs where pieces talk to each other.
LEARN_TRACK_EXPERT_BLURB: Pipelining, hazards, verification, SoC integration. The material from a Sistemas en Chip or Computer Architecture course.
LEARN_SAMPLE_TRY_BODY: Create a throw-away project seeded with this sample and jump straight to the workbench.
LEARN_SAMPLE_FIX_BODY: We give you a design that doesn't quite work. Open it, find the bug, make it build and simulate correctly.
LEARN_SAMPLE_PROJECT_BODY: Open the starter scaffold and build the design from there. Acceptance criteria and sample stimuli are in the reading above.
